statement: Raw images never leave a robot.
why_it_matters: Any idea requiring centralized frames is unusable.

statement: Safety alerts must remain below 80 ms p95.
why_it_matters: Always-on multi-pass inference would miss the alert deadline.

statement: Adaptation averages no more than 2.0 W over a shift.
why_it_matters: Heavy retraining shortens the operating shift.

statement: Each robot may upload at most 8 MB per day.
why_it_matters: Large checkpoints or gradients consume the entire link budget.

statement: All robots should converge toward one global model.
why_it_matters: Convergence can erase complementary specialists and correlate errors.

statement: Every site needs the same fixed label ontology.
why_it_matters: A shared ontology can hide locally meaningful failure distinctions.

statement: Adaptation begins only after labels arrive.
why_it_matters: Useful fleet signals appear many hours before labels.

statement: Useful collaboration must exchange data, gradients, or weights.
why_it_matters: Relational error summaries may be smaller and more diagnostic.

statement: Drift is a nuisance to erase, and forgetting is the primary objective.
why_it_matters: Recurrent regimes may reward recoverability rather than uniform retention.

statement: The learner is only the model on the robot.
why_it_matters: Location and peer state can carry adaptation memory.

statement: Model diversity is a temporary defect before synchronization.
why_it_matters: Diversity can create error complementarity.

statement: Old adapters are dead storage once a regime disappears.
why_it_matters: Dormant expertise can be cheaper to revive than relearn.

statement: A compressed gradient is the smallest meaningful collaboration unit.
why_it_matters: Sketches and signatures use far less bandwidth.

statement: Context belongs to the current robot session, not to a place or shift.
why_it_matters: Failures recur by zone and time across robots.

statement: One scalar forgetting score is a sufficient research objective.
why_it_matters: It conflates recurrent recovery with novel adaptation.

statement: The best peer is the robot from the most similar site.
why_it_matters: Error-signature compatibility is more predictive.

statement: Fleet adaptation requires a continuously available coordinator.
why_it_matters: Short peer messages remain available during coordinator outages.

statement: A fleet update must wait for synchronized rounds.
why_it_matters: Barriers are unavailable during simultaneous shifts.

statement: Inference must always finish in one pass.
why_it_matters: Sparse selective rechecking can fit the deadline.

statement: More replay is the safest path to robustness.
why_it_matters: Replay can exceed power and overwrite useful specialists.

statement: Uncertainty summaries are meaningful only with labels.
why_it_matters: The convention may suppress local specialization without satisfying a hard requirement.

statement: Evaluation windows remain fixed after deployment.
why_it_matters: The choice changes which failures are visible during evaluation.

statement: Site identity should be decided centrally.
why_it_matters: Relaxing it could permit asynchronous or relational coordination.

statement: Calibration thresholds must be identical across the fleet.
why_it_matters: Changing this boundary could alter what information the system treats as state.

statement: Peer selection must be globally comparable.
